paras: Cyrtodactylus sworderi, also known commonly as the Johore bow-fingered gecko, the Kota-tinggi forest gecko, and Sworder's bent-toed gecko, is a species of lizard in the family Gekkonidae. The species is endemic to Malaysia.
The specific name, sworderi, is in honor of Mr. Hope Sworder, who collected the holotype.
C. sworderi is known from the Malaysian state of Johor.
The preferred natural habitats of C. sworderi are desert and freshwater wetlands.
Adults of C. sworderi have a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 7–8 cm (2.8–3.1 in).
